$comment: Copy this to the root of the repository you want to gate, as slop.config.json.
include/exclude are globs relative to that root. Exclude test files: they are
not the code whose quality you are ratcheting, and including them lets a large
well-factored test suite mask erosion in the source.
thresholds are ratchet CEILINGS — lower is better, so they only ever move DOWN.
Start at null (report only), run `slopgate --report`, then write the measured
values in. Do not copy the paper's human-panel numbers here: those describe
Python repositories and are context, not a target.
calibratedAtRulePackVersion must match rules/VERSION. Adding slop rules can
only push verbosity up, so a stale value means the ceiling is measuring
something different from what it was set against, and the gate refuses to
compare rather than reporting a meaningless regression.
